title: Distributor deductions, disputed
brief:
A $4M natural-foods snack brand faces a month of **UNFI and KeHE deductions**.

**Disputed or questioned — $10,882:**
- Promotions deducted over the deal-sheet rate
- A shortage the delivery proof shows clean
- Spoils billed despite the agreement's allowance
- A duplicate SSA and a double event deduction
- Backup asked for on an unproven ad fee

**Left alone:**
- Promotions at the approved rate, KeHE's 8% fee
- Shortages noted on the delivery proof
- Billing ahead of a price change
- Free fill the agreement promised
- Items past each portal's window
promise: Every deduction UNFI and KeHE took matched against your deal sheets, agreement and proof of delivery — the invalid ones disputed with the evidence attached, the valid ones left alone, before the windows close.
persona: A $4M natural-foods snack brand selling through UNFI and KeHE, with a part-time finance person
chore: Each month the distributors pay less than they owe: promotions, shortages, spoils, fees, pricing. The brand pulls deductions from the myUNFI Dispute Center and KeHE's K-Solve, decodes each code, then hunts the evidence outside both portals — the broker's deal sheets, the distribution agreement, the warehouse's proof of delivery, the price-change letter — and disputes inside each portal's window. Small ones are written off because nobody has the hours; services that do it want the brand's portal logins and a cut.
command: Go through this month's UNFI and KeHE deductions, check each one against our deal sheets, agreement, price changes and proofs of delivery, dispute every one that's wrong with the evidence, ask for backup where we can't tell, and leave the valid ones alone.

apps.name: myUNFI Dispute Center
apps.role: UNFI deductions, the deduction key, disputes

apps.name: Brand Drive
apps.role: the broker's deal sheets, the distribution agreement, the price-change letter

apps.name: Warehouse portal
apps.role: proofs of delivery with receiver notes

steps: Reads each portal's own rules: windows, the SSA change, fees that are valid.
Lists the deductions in both portals, including KeHE items older than its quick search shows.
Pulls the deal sheet, the agreement clause, the price change or the proof of delivery each code needs.
Computes what was over-deducted, not just whether something was.
Disputes in each portal with the evidence named, asks for backup where the brand cannot tell, and leaves valid charges alone.

gates.label: Dispute a deduction
gates.why: It goes to the distributor's deductions team; a weak dispute costs credibility on the next one.

gates.label: Ask for backup
gates.why: It goes outside the company and starts the distributor's clock.

traps: A promotion deducted at the approved rate, plus KeHE's 8% fee — both valid.
A shortage the proof of delivery itself notes as short.
A pricing deduction where the brand billed the new price before it took effect.
A UNFI item older than twelve months, and a KeHE item past 180 days that only advanced search shows.
memory: Each deduction code and the evidence it needs, per distributor.
The deal calendar per retailer, cited to the broker's sheets.
Which warehouse's proofs of delivery carry receiver notes.
What was disputed and won, so the same code is argued the same way next month.

economics.basis: An estimate. Mid-market brands write off 1.2–2.4% of distributor revenue to deductions they never recover (a vendor figure, Overdeduct). For this example's $4M brand: $4,000,000 x 1.5% = $60,000 a year, inside the band's $48,000 to $96,000. For another brand, multiply its own distributor revenue by 1.2% to 2.4%: a maker with $45,600 a year of distributor sales would be at about $547 to $1,094. It fits brands selling through grocery distributors such as UNFI and KeHE, not makers selling through Faire or direct wholesale, where no distributor takes deductions. The bench world holds $10,882 across one month: $9,902 disputed on six deductions and $980 questioned for backup. The dispute windows (twelve months on UNFI, 180 days on KeHE) are as the cited sources described them on 7 October 2026; check each portal's current terms.
economics.incumbent: Deduction services want the brand's portal logins; SupplyPike calls 30% of recoveries the industry standard, Glimpse charges about $1,000 a month plus 10%. Brands under $5M mostly dispute nothing.

sources.label: SPS Commerce: UNFI's Dispute Center replaces email (2026)
KeHE and UNFI deduction codes and clocks
Glimpse: UNFI and KeHE supplier deductions guide (2026)
Confido: 10–15 hours a month just gathering deduction data (vendor)

edge.difficulty_why: Two distributor portals, a code key, evidence in two systems outside them, and amounts to recompute rather than accept.
edge.usefulness_why: Tens of thousands a year for a small brand, every month, that today mostly goes unclaimed.

expectation.why: A diligent finance person recovers most of it in a day; the bar is most of the money and no dispute of a valid charge.

caveat: Juniper Snacks Co, its broker and warehouse, every person and business here, and the four portals (modelled on the shape of myUNFI's Dispute Center, KeHE's K-Solve, a shared drive and a warehouse system) are invented; no deduction, price or contract is any real brand's. The public rules applied are the distributors' published dispute windows and deduction codes as the cited sources describe them (twelve months on UNFI, 180 days on KeHE, the approved promotion rate and KeHE's 8% fee), fixed in the bench world as of 7 October 2026. A real distributor's agreement, its current portal terms and the brand's own contracts decide real disputes differently. This applies stated rules to stated facts; it is not legal or financial advice.

fit.where_note: US grocery distributors' published dispute terms; other distributors and countries differ.
fit.who: A food or beverage brand selling through grocery distributors such as UNFI or KeHE that take deductions from what they pay.
fit.not_for: A maker selling through Faire, Etsy or direct wholesale, where no distributor takes deductions.
asks_for: the distributors' deduction lists or remittances
your broker's deal sheets and promotion approvals
proofs of delivery from your warehouse
fit.costs: No fees from Athena; only your Claude usage. Deduction services usually keep a share of what they recover.
